options.text: Radiation — heat reaches his hand from the heater without contact.
Conduction — heat passes only through contacting solid parts.
Convection — heater particles themselves move into his hand.
Conduction — any warmth from a heater is conduction.

stem:
The diagram shows Reyansh holding his hand beside a glowing room heater without touching it. His hand feels warm.

How does heat reach his hand?

teacher.key_rationale: Heat from the glowing heater reaches the hand without contact, which is radiation. Conduction needs contact through a solid; convection is movement of fluid particles, not solid heater bits into the hand.
teacher.figure_note: Glowing heater with heat reaching a nearby hand.
